# Test fixtures

`pink-5s.ogg`: five seconds of pink noise, mono, 44.1 kHz, encoded with
libvorbis at quality 3. Generated by this project for its own tests, no
third-party content:

    ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "anoisesrc=color=pink:sample_rate=44100:duration=5:amplitude=0.5:seed=7" \
        -c:a libvorbis -q:a 3 -page_duration 150000 pink-5s.ogg

It gives the Ogg chain-seam tests (`drain_test.go`) real Vorbis framing:
real lacing values and block sizes, the encoder's own header layout, ~33
pages of about 150 ms (near the ~4 KB pages a libogg-muxed file has).
Noise rather than a sine because a pure tone compresses to a dozen pages,
too few to place seams in.
